part: X1270WR-2x12A-6TV01 (LCSC C5147255) footprint, JLCPCB's own library (EasyEDA JSON) - J-MCU pin-1 cross-check
notes: Source: JLCEDA/EasyEDA official library (https://lceda.cn/, https://easyeda.com), contributor lcsc; package CONN-TH_24P-P1.27_XKB_X1270WR-2X12A-6TV01. Fetched with a browser User-Agent. USED FOR ONE THING: which end and row is pin 1. Units 10 mil, y down: pads odd 1..23 at y 2998, even 2..24 at y 3003, pin 1 (the RECT pad) at the +x end, the body's silk below the pads (+y), the silk pin-1 triangle beside pin 1 - so seen from above with the mouth toward the viewer, pin 1 is at the right and in the row FARTHER from the body, the same as the drawing's views (datasheets/connectors/XKB-X1270WR-2x12A-9TV01.pdf) read together with the 6TV01 STEP's key slot over that row. ITS TAIL ROWS ARE THE 6TV01's (0.55 and 1.82 behind the body), NOT the 9TV01 drawing's rev A1 (1.33 and 2.60): do not take tail positions from this file.

part: WS2815B-V1 (LCSC C5446699) footprint, JLCPCB's own library (EasyEDA JSON) - the assembler's pin 1 and rotation for D-LED
notes: Source: JLCEDA/EasyEDA official library (https://lceda.cn/, https://easyeda.com), contributor LCSC; package LED-SMD_6P-L5.0-W5.0-BR-RD-1, the footprint JLCPCB's placement preview draws for C5446699. Units 10 mil, y down. Pads numbered DIFFERENTLY from Worldsemi's sheet: left column 6, 4, 2 and right column 5, 3, 1, top to bottom; the chamfer (a filled document-layer triangle) and a silk corner mark are both at pad 1, bottom right. So JLC's pin 1 is the chamfered corner - Worldsemi's pin 4 (datasheets/led/WS2815B-V1.pdf p.2). At 0 deg its chamfer is bottom right; on hardware/lib/woody.pretty/LED_WS2815B-V1_PLCC6_5.4x5.0mm_P1.6mm at 0 deg it is top left: 180 deg apart, which the CPL's rotation (or the preview's correction) must carry.
